title: 归档旧的项目重规划与并发治理方案
summary: 已被当前这次只读审计、用户需求式管理架构和新的运行时稳定性方案取代。旧方案中的并发资源声明与分批恢复原则将作为后续实现输入，但不再保留一个独立元治理 Issue，也不会在切换后再次创建大规模 rebaseline 任务树。
goals: Wait for the simplified runtime architecture and failure-isolation gate before reopening downstream write work.
Reclassify all remaining active Issues and Tasks against the post-cutover source and Controller state.
Cancel, merge, narrow or supersede contracts invalidated by the new runtime architecture.
Define deterministic path/resource concurrency admission only after primary runtime ownership is simplified.
Prove bounded parallelism through staged pilots before reopening broader work.
Reopen product and optimization work in controlled priority waves.
nonGoals: Do not implement Supervisor, rollout, Recovery, runtime config or authority architecture in this Issue.
Do not preserve stale blue/green, mutable source, compatibility fallback or multi-writer assumptions.
Do not dispatch tasks merely because their historical status is ready.
Do not push, publish, tag or perform irreversible remote actions.
Do not delete dirty work or evidence without proven ownership and disposition.
acceptanceCriteria: ISS-20260802-539E7F reaches its fault-injection and cutover gates before portfolio reopening.
Every remaining active Issue is classified with a current reason and owning architecture dependency.
Duplicate, obsolete and partially superseded work is explicitly reconciled.
Concurrency admission covers repository, checkout, paths and global resources such as ports, Supervisor, Browser, devices and remote surfaces.
Read-only, one-writer and independent-writer pilots leave no checkout drift, unrelated commits or ghost leases.
Downstream work is reopened one wave at a time using refreshed contracts.
relatedArtifacts: new requirement-management and SQLite architecture Issue

tasks.title: Rebaseline remaining portfolio after runtime cutover
tasks.objective: After ISS-20260802-539E7F completes fault injection and staged cutover, audit every remaining active Issue, Task, Work, Run, Edit Session and dirty checkout against the new process, authority, config, release and Recovery architecture. Classify each as continue, revise, merge, preserve-history, supersede, cancel, blocked or ready.
acceptanceCriteria: Every active Issue has one current classification and owning dependency.
No old runtime/Recovery/tool-surface contract remains dispatchable without revalidation.
Dirty work and unique evidence are preserved and assigned before cleanup.
Duplicate and obsolete governance Issues are closed rather than nested.
notes: Blocked until ISS-20260802-539E7F completes T8 fault-injection gate and T9 staged cutover. This governance line must not run against the pre-refactor runtime.

tasks.title: Define post-simplification concurrency admission
tasks.objective: Define deterministic repository, checkout, path and global-resource claims for the simplified architecture. Supervisor, release activation, runtime config, Recovery, ports, Browser, simulator, device and remote mutation surfaces remain exclusive unless explicitly proven independent.
acceptanceCriteria: Admission uses concrete resources and paths rather than semantic guesswork.
Runtime/Recovery lifecycle resources are exclusive by default.
Base-revision change invalidates stale verification evidence.
Main remains controlled single-writer for integration.

tasks.title: Run bounded concurrency pilots
tasks.objective: Run staged pilots: parallel read-only work, one isolated writer plus readers, different-repository writers with no shared resources, and same-repository writers only if actual paths and global resources are disjoint. Measure drift, leases, evidence validity, commit scope, integration and cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: No wrong-checkout process or unrelated commit occurs.
No ghost lease or unexplained active state remains.
Failure at a pilot level restores the previous concurrency level.
Approved concurrency is backed by receipts, not assumptions.

tasks.title: Reopen downstream work in controlled waves
tasks.objective: Refresh and reopen the surviving Browser, Apple, iOS, repository workflow and product Issues one wave at a time using the post-cutover architecture and proven concurrency level. Do not recreate cancelled V2, source-identity, compatibility-heavy tool-surface or duplicate governance contracts.
acceptanceCriteria: Every reopened Task has a current contract and resource claims.
Only one delivery wave is opened at a time.
Cancelled architecture contracts are not recreated under new names.
Completed branches/worktrees are merged and cleaned promptly.
